items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: he happens to be responsible for everything that I'm saying here, because he's talked to me about it for some time and sort of been a catalyst in getting me to do this particular thing.

ctx.x: This is the 5th of May, 1983, up at John Malachi's house in Washington, D.C. This is John's interview for the Oral History Project. Take it away, John.

Thanks, Bryant. I guess I can start off by saying that I've really always seen music literally through the eyes of the piano. I guess that probably goes back to the days when I was fascinated by the keyboard on the old pump organ in my grandmother's house down in North Carolina, where I was born.

I was born in Red Springs, North Carolina, September 6, 1919. As a child, I used to wander into the living room, and they would put me up on the stool and just let me bang on the piano keys. At the same time, my mother used to take me to church, and my grandmother and all my aunts and everyone, they all went to church together. And they would all have a hymn book, singing.
